purpose: First-party Gef curriculum scaffold for deciding what kinds of communicative work to research at each CEFR band. These are not official CEFR descriptors and are not vocabulary lists.
rules: These targets define research territory, not mandatory words or grammar shared by every language.
A language-specific specification resolves these targets into real lexemes, senses, constructions, scripts, phonology, discourse conventions, and pragmatics.
Higher levels emphasize breadth, precision, discourse, register, inference, and domain flexibility rather than a finite checklist.
A target can appear at more than one level as independence, range, precision, and complexity increase.

research_domains: yes, no, thanks, greeting, leave-taking and other tiny social exchanges
script, sound or sign recognition needed to begin reading/listening
levels.independence_goal: Move from isolated recognition or memorized fragments toward tiny predictable exchanges with less support.
levels.reading_goal: Recognize a small dependable set of highly familiar forms and extract meaning when context is extremely supportive.

research_domains: days, dates, clock time and simple schedules
basic possession, existence, location, identity and description
short notices, labels, messages and highly predictable narrative
levels.independence_goal: Use a small repertoire productively instead of relying only on memorized whole phrases.
levels.reading_goal: Understand short, concrete material when vocabulary, syntax and context are highly familiar.

research_domains: invitations, arrangements and routine social coordination
short connected narrative and practical correspondence
levels.independence_goal: Handle familiar routine situations with less scripting and connect several simple ideas into a useful exchange.
levels.reading_goal: Follow the main point and useful details in short straightforward material on familiar subjects.

research_domains: media, hobbies, interests and cultural topics
summarizing the main point of accessible material
connected messages, stories, descriptions and informal argument
levels.independence_goal: Sustain connected communication through ordinary situations without another person or a translation tool carrying the structure.
levels.reading_goal: Follow central meaning across longer connected texts on familiar or personally relevant topics and infer some meaning from context.

research_domains: academic and professional communication in accessible domains
stance, emphasis and degrees of certainty
register differences across common formal and informal settings
implicit links across paragraphs or turns
idiomatic and figurative language that is common rather than highly specialized
levels.independence_goal: Communicate effectively at length with enough range to discuss complexity and repair many gaps without derailing the interaction.
levels.reading_goal: Understand substantial authentic material, including abstraction and argument, while using context and structure to manage unknown language.

research_domains: specialized academic or professional language by domain
rhetorical effect, hedging, emphasis and diplomacy
culturally situated pragmatic choices where evidence supports them
levels.independence_goal: Use language flexibly and deliberately across demanding contexts rather than merely cope with them.
levels.reading_goal: Follow demanding extended texts, including implicit relationships, stylistic choices and specialized material when the domain is reasonably accessible.

research_domains: fine semantic distinctions and near-synonym choice
rare or specialized language by domain rather than one global word list
dense figurative, ironic and allusive language
rapid synthesis across multiple difficult sources
precise reformulation under tight meaning constraints
historical, literary, technical or dialectal variation when relevant to the learner's goals
levels.independence_goal: Maintain exceptionally high precision, flexibility and control even when language, subject matter or style becomes unusually demanding.
levels.reading_goal: Handle extremely demanding texts with fine sensitivity to implication, structure and style while still using domain knowledge or reference tools when appropriate.
